resumen: The swing with one hand on the handle: the same hip snap, but the trunk has to resist the rotation caused by the load on one side.
ejecucion: Stand with your feet slightly wider than your hips and the kettlebell on the floor, a hand’s length in front, and grip it with one hand.
With a straight back, push your hips back and hike it back between your legs; the bell travels high, close to the groin.
Drive your hips forward hard so it swings up on a straight arm to chest height, shoulders square, without your torso rotating towards the kettlebell.
At the top, stand tall as in a plank, without leaning back; let it fall and repeat.
When you finish, let it lose momentum and set it down with a straight back; switch hands.
If your torso rotates or your back rounds at the bottom, go back to the two-handed swing.
matices: In a study of fourteen trained people, the one-arm swing activated the erectors more than the snatch and the vastus lateralis more than the clean. Another, in twenty-three people, measured two-handed and one-arm swings together and found gluteus maximus (around 75 %) and biceps femoris (79 %) activation of their maximum. With one hand, the load on one side also forces you to resist trunk rotation.
